marks.gloss_en: R' Yochanan: R' Yehuda and R' Elazar derive it from 'only be strong not to eat the blood': whatever you are commanded on its blood, on its limbs

whatever you are commanded concerning its blood, you are commanded concerning its limbs; these non-kosher ones too -- since you are commanded concerning their blood, you are commanded concerning their limbs
R' Yochanan: the Rabbis derive it from 'not the life with the flesh' -- but flesh alone
'you shall not eat the life with the flesh' -- but flesh alone; whatever whose flesh is permitted, you are commanded concerning its limbs, and whatever whose flesh is not permitted, you are not
תניא נמי הכי: the baraita gives the verse and the blood-to-limbs principle as 'the words of R' Elazar'
מאי טעמא דרבי מאיר? אמר קרא וזבחת מבקרך ומצאנך
what is R' Meir's reason? the verse says 'and you shall slaughter of your cattle and of your flock' (Deut 12:21)
תניא נמי הכי: a son of Noach is warned on non-kosher as on kosher, an Israelite only on kosher
the baraita: a limb from a living animal -- a son of Noach is warned concerning it in non-kosher as in kosher, and an Israelite is warned only concerning kosher ones
אף אנן נמי תנינא: 'slaughter does not render it pure' -- of the sons of Noach, by implication it is forbidden to them
the mishna: one who ate a limb from a living one of it is not flogged forty, and slaughter does not render it pure
מאי טעמא? אכילה כתיבה ביה
Rav: a limb from a living animal requires an olive-bulk
רמי רישא אסיפא -- he set the mishna's first clause [no forty lashes] against its last [slaughter does not render it pure]
ומשני: רישא בישראל, וסיפא בבן נח (= p_mani_reisha_seifa)
R' Mani bar Pattish: the first clause [no forty lashes] is of an Israelite, and the last clause [slaughter does not render it pure] of a son of Noach
מתיב רב עמרם: 'he is not flogged forty' -- and if you think an olive-bulk is required, let it follow that he ate an olive-bulk [and is flogged]
כדאמר רב נחמן: במשהו בשר גידין ועצמות; הכא נמי -- here too, a bit of meat, sinews and bones
תא שמע, דאמר רב: a kosher bird eaten alive -- for any amount
אילימא בישראל -- פשיטא דאין שחיטה מטהרתה
if we say [the mishna speaks] of an Israelite -- it is obvious that slaughter does not render it pure
let the prohibition of the limb come and take effect on the non-kosher prohibition, since its prohibition applies to the sons of Noach

the baraita: the limb prohibition applies to all, non-kosher and kosher, as it says 'only be strong not to eat the blood': whatever you are commanded concerning its blood you are commanded concerning its limbs -- the words of R' Elazar
the baraita: the Sages: it applies only to kosher species, as it says 'you shall not eat the life with the flesh' -- but flesh alone
R' Meir: it applies only to a kosher domestic animal
Rav: the dispute is concerning an Israelite
some say [the baraita reads] 'a kosher one' (singular), and it is R' Meir
